newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power steady to higher with cuts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power steady to higher with cuts.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Midwestern U.S. were steady to slightly higher for short term deals due to some transmission and generation cuts, brokers and marketers said.
Hourly power in the northern Mid-West was said to be trading higher due to some transmission curtailments out of the Canadian province of Manitoba, sources said.
The curtailments were expected to be short lived, however and little impact was seen on next-day pricing.
Also some talk of unit outages in the southern Mid-West pushed next-day prices up, the sources said.

In the East Central Area Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak, non-firm electricity prices for Friday delivery were seen trading higher near $17.00 from around $16.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Wednesday.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was talked steady in the $12.50-14.00 area, the sources said.
November ECAR prices were steady at $17.25-17.55, while December was quoted at $18.70-19.10. January/February ECAR business was assessed steady at $20.85-21.00 per MWh.

Peak, non-firm power prices for Friday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) were talked steady at $15.00-16.00, although hourly power climbed to near $17.00 with the Manitoba Hydro constraints, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was assessed steady at $8.00-10.00.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), non-firm peak power for Friday delivery was assessed higher at $16.50-18.00 from near $17.00 on Wednesday, the sources said.
Off-peak next day power was pegged steady in the $11.50-13.00 range.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in the entire region was pegged at 18.50-22.50 from $17.00-21.00 on Wednesday.
The price rise came with reports of several short-term generation outages and strong natural gas prices, the sources said.
Off-peak prices in SPP held steady in the $12.50-14.00 area.
November SPP was discussed near $18.50 in the north and $19.25 in the south, while December SPP was talked in the $22.25-22.50 range for the south region, the sources said.
Separately, Entergy said its 836 megawatt Arkansas 1 unit was expected to restart production from a scheduled maintenance outage late Saturday or early Sunday.
